title: His mother as pianist and taskmaster
summary: Collins credits his mother's immaculate taste and strictness; she led a trio and did rehearsal work at the Oriental and Chicago Theatres.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yes, right. So any way, I used to do this, and I had mentioned Dan Grissom. But he used to sing like Louis Armstrong, and my mother stopped him from singing like Louis Armstrong, he made him stop -- he had such a beautiful voice. But any way, he was working with us when he went with Lunceford. My mother had a little trio in Chicago, so I -- I keep bringing my mother up, but she was such a tremendous pianist and she was such a hard taskmaster, because if I would play wrong, anything wrong, she might hit me or anything. She was just -- oh, but we were inseparable. And I really attribute most of how I feel about music to my mother. You know, there's nothing -- her taste was immaculate. And her playing as far as I was concerned was immaculate, and I was a pretty good judge because I heard everybody.

And she also -- while we were in Chicago she also worked for the Oriental Theatre. She used to do like a rehearsal pianist. At this time they wouldn't have a colored pianist in a band or anything, in a white band, but she did all the rehearsal work for the Oriental Theatre and the Chicago Theatre. She was a fine musician.
